processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Electroslag remelted (ESR) material homogenized to eliminate probable segregation.
Hot rolled through 5 passes in the temperature range of 1100–1200 °C.
Hot rolling followed by air quenching.
Annealed to attain a triplex (ferrite + austenite + martensite) microstructure.
Compression specimens were soaked at deformation temperature for 5 min before testing to reach thermal equilibrium.
Compression at 500 °C under strain rate of 0.001 s^-1 up to true strain 0.6 using Gotech AI-7000 universal testing machine with a programmable furnace.
Specimens immediately water quenched to preserve the deformed high-temperature microstructure.

structures.overall_structure: Banded triplex (ferrite + austenite + thermally induced martensite) microstructure after warm compression at 500 °C, 0.001 s^-1, to true strain 0.6. Deformation bands are frequently distributed through the microstructure; the parent austenite is effectively sheared by propagation of the deformation bands; simultaneous deformation-induced ferrite→austenite and austenite→ferrite transformations occur along the deformation bands as a strain compensation mechanism.

phases_present.morphology: dominant green matrix carrying a banded structure with deformation bands
elongated bands along the compression axis plus blocky islands; effectively sheared by deformation bands
yellow/orange bands accompanying austenite; thermally induced from prior annealing
deformed ferrite matrix accommodating strain by multiple slip and banded structure development

defects.type: dislocation cell structures from tangled dislocations

phases_present.morphology: ferrite with cell structures and planar-slip-like character

defects.type: {110}<111> and {112}<111> slip traces (intersection of slip bands)

phases_present.morphology: fresh ferrite grains formed inside prior austenite

defect_interactions.interaction_type: intersection of {110}<111> and {112}<111> slip bands producing dislocation cells
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The strain within the ferrite is mainly accommodated through activation of multiple slip systems {110}<111> and {112}<111>; formation and intersection of slip bands is highly probable, and the wavy dislocation movement and high dislocation maneuverability favour formation of dislocation cells and high dislocation density walls (HDDWs).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: deformation band propagation shearing the parent austenite
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The parent austenite is effectively sheared through propagation of the deformation bands; the shear strain localization along the deformation bands is released through simultaneous austenite→ferrite and ferrite→austenite transformations as a strain compensation mechanism.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Within the ferrite, strain is accommodated mainly by activation of multiple slip systems {110}<111> and {112}<111>, giving a planar-slip-like character and intersection of slip bands (HDDWs, cell structures).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Simultaneous deformation-induced ferrite→austenite (DIFT) and austenite→ferrite (DIAT) transformations occur along the deformation bands at 500 °C, releasing shear strain localization, reducing flow localization and causing flow softening; bidirectional transformation is enabled by the equal Gibbs free energies of ferrite and austenite resulting from Al/Mn partitioning. Such transformations are not observed at 600 °C.
interfaces.interface_notes: Partial transformation to ferrite because the deformation-induced transformation during warm deformation proceeds via bidirectional ferrite/austenite interfaces; fresh ferrite forms inside parent austenite.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Specimens soaked at 500 °C for 5 min before testing; immediately water quenched after deformation. Compression axis (CA) marked in figure_002.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Compressive true stress–strain curve at 500 °C (0.001 s^-1): maximum flow stress near the 550–560 MPa level, followed by appreciable flow softening after a true strain of ~0.3.

characterization_methods.technique: Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FE-SEM CZ/MIRA I LMH, TESCAN, Czech; EBSD detector Hikari, AMETEK EDAX, USA
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural characterization, phase mapping (BCC/FCC), triplex phase separation, deformation band imaging
characterization_methods.key_findings: Revealed banded triplex (ferrite-martensite-austenite) microstructure; deformation bands are denser and more frequently distributed at 500 °C than 600 °C.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM: JEM-2100-F, acceleration voltage 200 kV, field-emission gun (JEOL Ltd, Japan); thin foils by twin-jet polishing in HClO4 (10%) + methyl alcohol (90%) at -30 °C, 16 V
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Bright-field imaging and SAED, at interrupted strain 0.3 and deformed microstructure
characterization_methods.purpose: Dislocation configuration, slip traces, cell structures, formation of fresh ferrite grains within parent austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite contains HDDWs, tangled dislocations and intersecting {110}/{112} slip traces; fresh ferrite grains form inside parent austenite; SAED patterns index ferrite (Z=[113]) and austenite (Z=[1-11]).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: After deformation at 500 °C, 0.001 s^-1, up to true strain 0.6
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Mn and Al partitioning between ferrite and austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite contains Mn 10.3 ± 0.1 wt% and Al 6.0 ± 0.1 wt%; austenite contains Mn 12.8 ± 0.1 wt% and Al 4.7 ± 0.1 wt%; Mn partitions to austenite and Al to ferrite.

characterization_methods.technique: High-temperature compression testing with flow curve acquisition and subsequent stress-strain extraction
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Gotech AI-7000 universal testing machine equipped with a programmable furnace
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Temperature 100–700 °C (this sample 500 °C), strain rate 0.001 s^-1, true strain 0.6
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine flow behavior and flow softening; extract maximum flow stress and yield stress vs temperature
characterization_methods.key_findings: 500 °C curve peaks near 550–560 MPa then softens; mechanical stability over 200–500 °C; significant stress drop from 500 to 600 °C; appreciable flow softening after true strain 0.3.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium calculation for Fe-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.07C system; isothermal sections at 500 and 550 °C; nominal composition line indicated. Phases considered: BCC_A2 (ferrite), FCC_A1 (austenite), BCC_A1#2 (high-Mn BCC).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Thermo-Calc predicted Mn/Al partitioning is 'almost similar' to the SEM-measured partitioning after deformation at 500 °C (Table 1); applying the nominal composition gives different Gibbs energies for ferrite and austenite at 500 °C, but using the partitioned compositions the same Gibbs free energy is obtained for both phases, supporting the bidirectional transformation.

analytical_models.equation_role: Interpret the kinetics/thermodynamics of phase transformation in the multicomponent alloying system; point A denotes composition where BCC and FCC have equal Gibbs energy.

parameters.name: Gibbs free energy equal point (A) composition, 500 °C, vs %Mn
Gibbs free energy at point A, 500 °C

analytical_models.model_note: Mn partitioning mainly dictates the Gibbs free energy and phase stability; over the whole Al% range the BCC and FCC Gibbs energies are nearly the same, so Al content has little effect on phase stability. The equal Gibbs energies (due to Al/Mn partitioning) provide the driving force for simultaneous DIFT and DIAT at 500 °C.

unmapped_findings: SEM-measured composition of the experimented steel after deformation at 500 °C, 0.001 s^-1, to true strain 0.6: ferrite contains Mn 10.3 ± 0.1 wt% and Al 6.0 ± 0.1 wt%; austenite contains Mn 12.8 ± 0.1 wt% and Al 4.7 ± 0.1 wt% (all values ±0.1 wt%); Mn partitions to austenite and Al to ferrite.

Compressive flow behaviour at 500 °C (0.001 s^-1, up to true strain 0.6): maximum flow stress reaches ~550–560 MPa; the flow curve shows mechanical stability similar to the 200–500 °C range, then appreciable flow softening after true strain ~0.3, attributed to strain-induced transformations rather than dynamic recrystallization/dynamic recovery.
The material is a ferrite-based low density (lightweight) steel with high stacking fault energy of 80–110 mJ/m^2 (alloy-level context relevant to the absence of TRIP/martensite transformation).

The deformation at 500 °C produced a banded structure that was not observed at 600 °C, because the higher temperature provides a greater capability for strain distribution; bidirectional transformations were also not characterized in the 600 °C-deformed microstructure.

The triplex starting microstructure (ferrite + austenite + thermally induced martensite) was produced by annealing at 950 °C/1 h; martensite and ferrite were distinguished using band-slope phase contrast since both have BCC crystal structure.
